cards.title: Russian and Ukrainian strikes keep civilian protection in focus
cards.summary: AP reported fresh Russian and Ukrainian attacks after a deadly strike on a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih; casualty totals remain time-sensitive.
detail: Associated Press reported that Russian drone and missile strikes killed people in Ukraine while a Ukrainian drone attack killed three people in Russia’s Krasnodar region. The report followed a Russian strike on a Kryvyi Rih shopping centre that Ukrainian officials said killed at least 16 people and wounded more than 130.

The immediate significance is the continuing civilian cost alongside the military exchange. The figures are reported by local and national authorities through AP, while the sequence of attacks shows why rescue access and air-defence capacity remain central to the conflict’s human consequences.

The next reliable signal is an updated official casualty count and independent confirmation of damage and responsibility. The two sides’ claims about targets and military effect remain attributed rather than settled facts.
cards.why: It is the clearest overnight international development with a verified civilian-protection consequence.

analysis: The story combines a diplomatic pressure signal with a separate humanitarian accountability dispute; both remain unresolved.
uncertainty: The scope and implementation of any economic action, safe-navigation arrangement, or independent investigation were not established in the checked sources.
conflicts: The reported positions are claims by the parties and do not independently establish responsibility for the underlying attacks.

cards.summary: The Generalitat lists organised viewing guidance for Aug. 12, while the University of Valencia provides a live broadcast and safety information.
detail: The Generalitat identifies Aug. 12, 2026 as a total solar eclipse visible across much of the Region of Valencia and advises visitors to check parking and capacity at official viewing points. The University of Valencia has organised public science activities and a live retransmission.

The useful next check is the same-day traffic, weather, fire-risk, and access notice from the authorities. If the low western horizon or cloud cover blocks a local view, the university stream is the clearest verified fallback.

cards.summary: The S&P 500 gained 0.4% and the Dow 1% on Friday, but the main U.S. indexes still finished the week lower.
detail: AP and Reuters reported that U.S. stocks rose on Friday while the bond market continued to pressure sentiment. The S&P 500 closed at 7,674.37, the Dow at 53,277.01 and the Nasdaq at 26,180.46.

The movement was a relief day inside a weaker week: Reuters reported weekly declines for all three major indexes, while AP highlighted the continued rise in yields and the role of earnings and services activity.
The next session will test whether lower-risk pressure eases. These are time-stamped market descriptions, not a forecast or investment recommendation.

The driver is mixed rather than directional: policy support can calm yields, but higher oil prices and uncertainty around the Iran war can reinforce inflation concerns. The sources describe the forces without establishing a settled policy outcome.

cards.summary: European benchmarks were broadly steady or firmer on Friday, but the week remained negative as borrowing costs and oil weighed on sentiment.
detail: Reuters and AP both described a steadier Friday session alongside a difficult week for markets. AP reported gains in much of Europe and Asia, while Reuters linked the broader weekly loss to fluctuating bond yields and higher oil.

The market signal is therefore a session rebound inside a more defensive weekly backdrop. Higher long-term yields matter because they raise financing costs and compete with equities for investors’ attention.
